query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Embedding an interconnected 10 vol% ductile copper network into the porous MnNiSi₀.₆₂(FeCoGe)₀.₃₈ alloy by powder‐metallurgical infiltration will raise its compressive strength to ≥300 MPa while retaining ≥90% of its original adiabatic temperature change (ΔTad) under a 2 T magnetic field at the transformation temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk MnNiSi₀.₆₂(FeCoGe)₀.₃₈ high‐entropy alloy with poor integrity (baseline compressive strength ≈50 MPa, baseline ΔTad under 2 T ≡ ΔT₀).
generation.intervention: Introduce 10 vol% interconnected Cu phase via molten‐Cu infiltration into a sintered, porous HEA preform.
generation.conditions: Measurements at 300 K ±10 K under a 2 T applied magnetic field; quasi‐static uniaxial compression up to 500 MPa at 10⁻³ s⁻¹ strain rate.
generation.structural_mediator: Ductile copper network bridging HEA grains and toughening grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The ductile Cu phase arrests crack initiation and propagation by stress redistribution and plastic accommodation; its high thermal conductivity preserves rapid heat flow so that the martensitic/ferro‐magnetic transition responsible for the caloric effect remains effectively unchanged.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compressive strength increases from ≈50 MPa to ≥300 MPa; ΔTad under 2 T remains ≥0.9·ΔT₀.
generation.baseline: Pristine MnNiSi₀.₆₂(FeCoGe)₀.₃₈: ≈50 MPa compressive strength; ΔTad under 2 T = ΔT₀.
generation.boundary: Valid for 2 T fields at 290–310 K, quasi‐static loading (strain rate ≤10⁻³ s⁻¹), Cu volume fractions ≈10 ± 2 %
generation.uncertainty: Exact optimal Cu fraction and resulting property trade-off may vary by ±2 vol% and ±10% in strength or caloric retention.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two samples: (i) baseline MnNiSi₀.₆₂(FeCoGe)₀.₃₈; (ii) identical alloy with 10 vol% Cu infiltration. Measure compressive strength at 300 K and ΔTad under 2 T at the transformation temperature.
measurements: Compressive stress–strain curve to determine 0.2% offset yield and max stress
Direct adiabatic ΔT measurement under 2 T
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the composite’s compressive strength <250 MPa or its ΔTad <0.8·ΔT₀ under the same 2 T field, the hypothesis is falsified.
